Content:
Multiplying any number by zero always equals zero. Below are some examples.

Content:
- [MATH: 5 \times 0 = 0]
- [MATH: 123\times 0 = 0]
- [MATH: -314\,159 \times 0 = 0]
- [MATH: 0\times 0 = 0]

Content:
To see why multiplying any number by zero always equals zero, let's take a look at the multiplication table for [MATH: 5], shown below.

Content:
[MATH: 5 × 4|= 20; 5 × 3|= 15; 5 × 2|= 10; 5 × 1|= 5; 5 × 0|= ◻?]

Content:
As we go down the list, the number in blue is reduced by [MATH: 5] each time. Following this pattern, we must have [MATH: \color{blue}\square = 0].

Content:
Note that, since multiplication is commutative, multiplying zero by any number (including itself) equals zero as well. Some examples are shown below.

Content:
- [MATH: 0 \times 5 = 0]
- [MATH: 0 \times 123 = 0]
- [MATH: 0 \times -314\,159 = 0]
- [MATH: 0 \times 0 = 0]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Multiplying any number by zero always equals zero. Below are some examples.

Content:
- [MATH: 5 \times 0 = 0]
- [MATH: 123\times 0 = 0]
- [MATH: -314\,159 \times 0 = 0]
- [MATH: 0\times 0 = 0]

Content:
To see why multiplying any number by zero always equals zero, let's take a look at the multiplication table for [MATH: 5], shown below.

Content:
[MATH: 5 × 4|= 20; 5 × 3|= 15; 5 × 2|= 10; 5 × 1|= 5; 5 × 0|= ◻?]

Content:
As we go down the list, the number in blue is reduced by [MATH: 5] each time. Following this pattern, we must have [MATH: \color{blue}\square = 0].

Content:
Note that, since multiplication is commutative, multiplying zero by any number (including itself) equals zero as well. Some examples are shown below.

Content:
- [MATH: 0 \times 5 = 0]
- [MATH: 0 \times 123 = 0]
- [MATH: 0 \times -314\,159 = 0]
- [MATH: 0 \times 0 = 0]
